entry.title: [Microsoft.Extensions.Validation] Microsoft Security Advisory CVE-2026-118749 - ASP.NET Core Denial of Service Vulnerability
entry.content:
Executive summary

Microsoft is releasing this security advisory to provide information about a vulnerability in ASP.NET Core. This advisory provides guidance on updating affected applications and components.

Minimal API validation repeatedly copies a growing validation-error dictionary, allowing attacker-controlled collections to trigger quadratic CPU work after the client disconnects.

Announcement

Announcement for this issue can be found at https://github.com/dotnet/announcements/issues/505

CVSS Details

  • Version: 3.1
  • Severity: High
  • Score: 7.5 (base score)
  • Vector: CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:N/UI:N/S:U/C:N/I:N/A:H/E:U/RL:O/RC:C
  • Weakness: CWE-407

Affected Platforms

  • Platforms: Windows, Linux, macOS
  • Architectures: All

Affected Packages

The tables list affected version ranges and fixed package versions. Runtime and standalone deliveries are listed separately.

.NET 11.0 - affected runtime packages

How do I know if I am affected?

Check the deployed runtime and application package versions against the affected ranges above. Self-contained applications include their own runtime; updating a machine-wide runtime does not replace it.

Install the applicable runtime or update each independently referenced package to the fixed version above. Restart applications. If you have found a potential security issue in a supported version of .NET, please report it to the Microsoft Security Response Center (MSRC) via the MSRC Researcher Portal. Further information can be found in the MSRC Report an Issue FAQ.

Security reports made through MSRC may qualify for the Microsoft .NET Bounty. Details of the Microsoft .NET Bounty Program including terms and conditions are at https://aka.ms/corebounty.

Support

You can ask questions about this issue on GitHub in the .NET GitHub organization. The main repos are located at https://github.com/dotnet/runtime. The Announcements repo (https://github.com/dotnet/Announcements) will contain this bulletin as an issue and will include a link to a discussion issue. You can ask questions in the linked discussion issue.
